lines.text: Do you know how a toaster knows when to pop? It's a spring, a magnet, and a little timer.
Pushing the lever down stretches a spring and closes a switch, so current flows.
Thin nichrome wires glow red hot, hundreds of degrees, and toast the bread with infrared heat.
An electromagnet holds the lever down, while a simple timer counts. The darkness dial just changes how long.
When time is up, the magnet lets go, the spring snaps back, and up comes your toast.
Older toasters used a strip of two metals that bends as it heats, and trips the catch instead.
